<thought>Based on the mass spectrum (monoisotopic [M+H]⁺ = 183.045, indicating a neutral mass ≈ 182.04 Da) and the ¹³C NMR data (a carbonyl carbon at ~169 ppm, six aromatic carbons, a benzylic CH₂ at ~43 ppm and a methyl carbon at ~26 ppm), the most consistent molecular formula is C₁₀H₁₁ClO. A structure that fits this formula and the NMR pattern is a chlorophenyl‑propyl‑ketone: a 4‑chlorophenyl group attached to a –CH₂‑CH₂‑C(=O)‑CH₃ chain. The corresponding SMILES is **Clc1ccc(cc1)CC(=O)C**. This provides one carbonyl (≈169 ppm), six aromatic carbons, a benzylic CH₂ (≈43 ppm) and a terminal methyl (≈26 ppm), matching the observed data.</thought>
<final_answer>Clc1ccc(cc1)CC(=O)C</final_answer>
